back: A system that controls the motion of a machine using an electric motor: source, power modulator, motor, load, control and sensing.
Power source, power modulator (converter), motor, mechanical load, control unit with sensors.
One motor drives several machines through a line shaft. Cheap, but one fault stops everything.
Each machine has its own motor.
Each mechanism of one complex machine has its own motor, e.g. rolling mills, paper machines.
Comes from gravity or stored energy (hoists, lifts). Keeps its direction when motion reverses.
Always opposes motion: friction, cutting, windage.
$T = C\,T_r\left(\frac{n}{n_r}\right)^k$, with $k = 0$ (hoist), $1$, $2$ (fan, pump), $-1$ (constant power).
$T_m - T_L = J\,\dfrac{d\omega_m}{dt}$
$\dfrac{dT_L}{d\omega} > \dfrac{dT_m}{d\omega}$ at the operating point.
$n \propto 1/\sqrt{T}$: high starting torque, speed falls steeply. Never run unloaded.
Forward motoring: $+\omega$, $+T$.
Forward braking: $+\omega$, $-T$.
Reverse motoring: $-\omega$, $-T$.
Reverse braking: $-\omega$, $+T$, e.g. lowering a heavy hoist load.
$E_b > V$: the motor generates and returns energy to the supply.
Armature disconnected from the supply and connected across a resistor; energy burnt as heat.
Supply reversed while running. Fast, but wastes the most energy; must disconnect at zero speed.
$\theta = \theta_{ss}\left(1 - e^{-t/\tau}\right) + \theta_0 e^{-t/\tau}$
$\tau = C/D$: thermal capacity over heat dissipation rate.
Continuous, short-time, intermittent periodic, and their variations (S1 to S8).
$I_{eq} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sum I_k^2 t_k}{\sum t_k}}$
A flywheel stores energy at light load and releases it at peak load to smooth the supply demand.
$V_a = \dfrac{2V_m}{\pi}\cos\alpha$ (continuous conduction)
Two full converters back to back: four-quadrant operation of a DC motor.
$N_s = \dfrac{120f}{P}$
$s = \dfrac{N_s - N}{N_s}$
Keep $V/f$ constant below base speed to hold the flux; above base speed $V$ is capped and the flux weakens.
Raises the slip for maximum torque; poor efficiency because slip power is burnt in the resistors.
A DC–DC converter: converts power directly from DC to DC.
$V_o = \delta E$ (step-down)
$V_o = \dfrac{E}{1-\delta}$ (step-up)
$|V_o| = \dfrac{\delta E}{1-\delta}$, inverted
$L_{crit} = \dfrac{(1-\delta)TR}{2}$
$L_c = \dfrac{RT}{2}\,\delta(1-\delta)^2$

front: Why use a starter on a 3-phase IM?
back: It is self-starting; the starter limits the heavy starting current and gives overload and no-voltage protection.
Full voltage at once. 6–8 × rated current, 0.75–2 × full-load torque. Motors below about 5 kW.
Start in star ($V_L/\sqrt3$ per phase), run in delta. Starting current and torque fall to 1/3.
Line current $= x^2 I_{sc}$ for tapping $x$. Works with star or delta motors.
